QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_19

question.text: The High-Water Mark (HWM) of a Category III AIF is:

answer.text: The highest NAV (net of operating expenses, transaction expenses and management fees) achieved by the fund at year-end
The peak GNAV during any hour
The initial subscription price plus GST

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 6.1.3, HWM = highest NAV (net of operating expenses, transaction expenses and management fees) at year-end. The Trap: Leverage, peak intra-day GNAV, and subscription price alone are not HWM definitions. Cross-Exam Context: Same HWM concept used in hedge fund industry globally. Distributor's Pro-Tip: HWM combined with hurdle delivers the tightest fee structure for investors.
